SMTO-CFG-0011 — The Gateway couldn't start: its working folder doesn't exist

GUID: 51919760-ea86-4f18-9add-647689f2e7b0
Slug: gateway-config-gateway-workdir-does-not-exist
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer, stopped right after starting. The folder it was told to run commands in can't be found on that computer. No files or settings were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Copy the folder path from the error message and check on the Gateway's computer whether that folder is there. The message names the exact folder the Gateway looked for, so you can see whether it was moved, renamed or deleted.
  2. If the folder was moved or renamed, or is on a drive or network share that isn't connected, put it back or reconnect it. The Gateway starts normally once the folder is where its setting says.
  3. Otherwise, change GATEWAY_WORKDIR in the command or settings used to start the Gateway to a folder that exists. For SMTO's built-in LocalMachine Gateway, ask the person who manages SMTO instead. The Gateway runs commands in this folder, so it must point somewhere real. LocalMachine uses the folder SMTO itself was started from.
  4. Start the Gateway again. Then open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection on that Gateway. This shows whether the Gateway now starts with the corrected value and SMTO can reach it.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway keeps running after it starts, and in Settings › Setup › Gateways it shows Connected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details (or copy the error shown where the Gateway was started) and send it, with the folder path, to the person who set up this Gateway. Don't create an empty folder with that name if your project files used to be there; find where they went first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway settings validation resolved the configured workdir (GATEWAY_WORKDIR, or the Server's workspace root for the built-in LocalMachine Gateway) and that path does not exist on the Gateway host.

What this means

  • A configured workdir is resolved on the Gateway host and exists() reports false. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • A configured workdir is resolved on the Gateway host and exists() reports false.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the resolved GATEWAY_WORKDIR on that host and its service-account visibility before creating or selecting a directory.

How to fix it

  • Point GATEWAY_WORKDIR (expanded and resolved on the Gateway host) at an existing directory the Gateway's OS account can access, or restore or remount the missing path; for the built-in LocalMachine Gateway the path is the Server's workspace root. Restart the Gateway afterwards.
  • Set GATEWAY_WORKDIR to an existing directory accessible by the Gateway service account. Restore the directory or its OS permissions before restarting the Gateway.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended existing directory resolves and passes subsequent directory/access checks.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
